_about: Mod Studio's prompt builder tasks. Edit or add tasks here; the page reloads this file. {name} fills in a fact about the selected mod (see studio/server.py mod_context): mod, title, version, target, app_version, dump_state, switches, works, fails, untested, hooks, log_errors, ask, extra, region. needs: what the task must have; a missing one shows a hint instead of a weak prompt.
limits: Limits: single-player features only; never hook purchases, ads, accounts or online play (list them under FLAGS instead); don't commit, publish or push without asking.
where: Project: Accretion mods. Target: AccretionMods/mods, mods/{mod} ({title} {version}) for {target} {app_version}. Dump: {dump_state}. Switches: {switches}.

tasks.label: Add a feature
tasks.ask: Which feature? (one line, e.g. player takes no damage)
lines: Goal: add "{ask}" to {title} as a switch (or slider) in the mod menu.
{where}

How: find the code that decides it (am find {mod} with regexes, am fields on the classes), prefer a no-JIT pin or call over a hook that needs JIT, then am add / am pin with a clear title, am build {mod} --ipa --bump and am run {mod}.
Done when: the switch changes the game on the phone (say what you saw in the log or on screen) and it is marked with am mark {mod} <key> --works or --fails.
If two ways look equally good, show both in two lines each and ask me before changing files.
{limits}

tasks.label: Narrow down the best approach
tasks.ask: For what? (one line: the feature or problem)
lines: Goal: pick the best way to do "{ask}" in {title}, before changing anything.
{where}

Give 2 to 4 approaches (hook a method, pin a field without JIT, call a method every few seconds, patch an offset). For each: what it touches (Class.method or Class.field from the dump), needs JIT or not, how likely it survives a game update, side effects, effort.
Recommend one with the reason, the exact am commands to try it, and how to check it on the phone.
Read only: change no files; wait for my choice.
{limits}

tasks.label: Explore the dump for tweaks
tasks.ask: Focus (optional: an area like currency, combat, timers; empty = everything)
lines: Goal: find the most promising tweaks in {title}'s dump{extra}, and flag the risky code.
{where}

How: am status {mod}; am suggest {mod} --no-pick; am find {mod} with regexes per area (currency|gold|coins|gems, health|hp|damage|armor, cooldown|timer|duration|speed, xp|level|exp, drop|loot|chance|rarity, unlock|owned|isLocked, energy|stamina); am fields on the classes that hold the values.

Deliver: a table by area (Class.method or Class.field, what changing it does, hook / pin / call, needs JIT, risk); FLAGS (purchase/IAP, ads, online/server, anti-cheat or integrity checks, cloud save); the top 10 ranked with the exact am add / am pin command each, skipping what the mod already has.
Read only: change no files.
{limits}

tasks.label: Fix a broken switch or crash
tasks.ask: What goes wrong? (one line: switch key or what you saw)
lines: Goal: fix this in {title}: "{ask}".
{where}
Switches marked fails: {fails}. Not yet checked on the phone: {untested}.
Last device log errors from Mod Studio: {log_errors}
How: find the cause first (am log {mod} --seconds 90 --launch, am check {mod}, the hook's signature in the dump), change the smallest thing, then am build {mod} --ipa --bump and am run {mod}.
Done when: the log shows no error for it and the switch is marked works on the phone; say what the cause was in one line.
{limits}

tasks.label: Update to the newest game
lines: Goal: bring {title} up to the newest App Store version of {target}, with every switch still working.{extra}
{where}

Steps: am games info {target} for the store version; am fetch --mod {mod} for a decrypted copy; am update {mod}; fix every hook it reports changed or missing (am find / am fields, then am add or am pin); am build {mod} --ipa --bump; am run {mod}.
Done when: each switch is marked works or fails on the new version (am mark), mod.json's tested_app_version is the new version, and you list what changed.
{limits}

tasks.label: Start a mod for another game
lines: Goal: start a personal mod for {ask}, using what worked in {title}.
Project: Accretion mods. Target: AccretionMods/mods, a new mods/<name>. Reference: mods/{mod} ({switches}).

Steps: am games info {ask} (version, engine hints, online flags); am fetch {ask} for a decrypted copy; am new <name> <the .ipa>; am dump <name>; am suggest <name> --no-pick for methods like the ones that worked before; propose the first 5 switches with commands and wait for my pick.
Done when: the mod folder exists, the dump is made, and you list the 5 proposed switches.
{limits}

tasks.label: Check before publishing
lines: Goal: tell me if {title} {version} is ready to publish, and what to fix first.{extra}
{where}

Check: every switch marked works on {app_version} (fails: {fails}; untested: {untested}); am check {mod} clean; no hook touches purchases, ads or online play; mod.json title, description, version and tested_app_version right; the .ipa builds (am build {mod} --ipa) and installs.
Deliver: ready / not ready, then a short list of blockers and nice-to-haves. Read only: change no files; publishing is my call (scripts/upload_ipa.ps1).
{limits}
